title: They Did Not Expect Him
source: State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow (public domain). Also known as Unexpected Visitors. Wikimedia Commons file: Ilya Repin Unexpected visitors.jpg (2740 x 2630 px)
caption: A thin, ragged man walks into a family's living room. Each person reacts differently. Who recognises him first? #homecoming #family #repin #fineart #storytime
_verify: VERIFIED 2026-10-17, Wikipedia EN (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/They_Did_Not_Expect_Him): 1884-1888, oil on canvas 160.5 x 167.5 cm, Tretyakov Gallery; an exile returns home, most likely a member of Narodnaya Volya back from a remote region of Russia; mother rises from her armchair toward her son and pushes a chair aside; wife at the piano, 'hesitant' joy; boy at the table (model Sergei Kostychev); young girl probably unaware of who the man is (model: Repin's eldest daughter Vera); maid with wary astonishment; Repin changed the exile's expression and head tilt at least three times, revisiting it in 1887 and 1888; final expression questioning, uncertain, mixing heroism and suffering; wall: portraits of Nekrasov and Shevchenko, Christ on Golgotha, Alexander II on his deathbed after his assassination by the Narodniki.

VERIFIED 2026-10-17, Vokrug Sveta (vokrugsveta.ru/article/246306/): political prisoner released early turns up unannounced (amnesties of the early 1880s); in 1887, while Tretyakov was away, Repin came to the gallery with paints and repainted the head; Tretyakov was furious; Repin reworked it again the next year; girl frightened, probably too young to remember her father; Nekrasov and Shevchenko as the Narodniki's inspirers; photograph of Alexander II in his coffin (killed 1881). Also gw2ru.com (Russia Beyond) on the 1887 gallery repainting: Tretyakov 'enraged'.
SOURCE NUANCE: Wikipedia says Alexander II on his deathbed, Vokrug Sveta says in his coffin. Slide 7 says only 'lying dead'.
INTERPRETATION: that the boy recognises his father is a common reading, not stated by Wikipedia (which says the boy adds warmth and life). Slide 6 says 'seems to recognise'.

SOURCE CONFLICT, not used: models for the mother (Wikipedia: Repin's wife Vera and Varvara Komarova; Vokrug Sveta: Repin's mother-in-law Yevgenia Shevtsova). The model for the man (Vsevolod Garshin) is 'thought to be', not used on slides.
UNVERIFIED, not used: Siberia as the place of exile (sources say only a remote region); how many years he was away (slide 9 asks a hypothetical question instead).
Not used (word budget): mother and wife both wear black, which Vokrug Sveta reads as mourning; Tretyakov bought it for 7,000 rubles.
Focus boxes estimated from the contact-sheet thumbnail; re-tune on the real image (the wife by the piano and which wall picture is which are the least certain).

slides.headline: A stranger walks into the living room
slides.sub: Ilya Repin, They Did Not Expect Him, 1884-1888

slides.headline: Russia, 1880s
slides.text: A quiet family afternoon: homework on the table, music on the piano. Then the door opens, and a thin, ragged man walks in.

slides.headline: Back from exile
slides.text: He's a political exile, most likely a revolutionary, back from a remote corner of the empire. Nobody knew he was coming home.

slides.headline: His mother rises
slides.text: First, the woman in black rises from her armchair, pushing it aside. She's his mother, and her whole body leans towards him.

slides.headline: His wife hesitates
slides.text: Behind her, by the piano, his wife turns. Her joy is still hesitant, as if she can't quite believe her eyes.

slides.headline: Two children, two reactions
slides.text: Then the children. The boy's face lights up: he seems to recognise his father. His little sister looks wary, probably too young to remember him.

slides.headline: Clues on the wall
slides.text: And look at the wall: poets Nekrasov and Shevchenko, heroes of young radicals, and Tsar Alexander II, assassinated by revolutionaries in 1881, lying dead.

slides.headline: A face repainted
slides.text: Look at his face again. Repin reworked it at least three times, once in the gallery while the owner was away. The owner was furious.

slides.headline: Who would know you?
slides.text: The final face is uncertain: half hero, half broken man, wondering if he still belongs here. If you vanished for years, who'd recognise you first?
